# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Security fixes are made on the `main` branch. The public production service is
supported only at its currently deployed release; older commits, local forks and
unofficial deployments are not supported.

## Report a vulnerability privately

Please use GitHub's **Security** tab and select **Report a vulnerability**. This
creates a private security advisory visible only to the reporter and the
repository maintainers.

Do not open a public issue, discussion or pull request for a suspected
vulnerability. Do not include credentials, access tokens, personal data or data
copied from production in a report. If the private reporting form is unavailable,
open a public issue that contains no vulnerability details and asks a maintainer
to establish a private channel.

Include, when possible:

- the affected component and release or commit;
- a concise description of the weakness and its potential impact;
- reproducible steps or a minimal proof of concept using synthetic data;
- prerequisites and any suggested mitigation;
- whether the issue is known to be actively exploited.

## What to expect

We aim to acknowledge a report within two business days, complete initial triage
within seven calendar days and provide a status update at least every fourteen
days until resolution. Remediation and disclosure timing depend on severity,
exploitability and the safety of deploying a fix.

Please allow a reasonable remediation period before public disclosure. We will
credit reporters who request attribution, unless legal or privacy constraints
prevent it.

## Good-faith research

Limit testing to accounts and data you own or have explicit permission to use.
Avoid privacy violations, service disruption, denial of service, social
engineering, automated high-volume traffic and attempts to access or retain other
people's data. Stop testing and report immediately if you encounter sensitive or
personal data.

Good-faith research that follows this policy will not be intentionally pursued as
an attack by the project maintainers. This statement does not grant permission to
test third-party infrastructure and cannot bind third parties or law enforcement.
